text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The prosecutor's office said both state minister of education Juris Celmins and state minister of health care Juris Vinkelis broke an anti-corruption law by having official and private posts at the same time but no criminal actions will be brought. Celmins is likely to stay in his post but the fate of Vinkelis was not clear.
- The economics ministry published an optimistic forecast for this year, predicting 4-5 percent GDP growth, low inflation of about 8 percent and an increase in purchasing power.
- Parliament passed amendments to the budget increasing revenues and expenditures by 26 million lats.
- Parliament passed in the final reading a law on the status of refugees and asylum seekers and ratified the 1951 convention on refugees.

- The U.S. congress has again voiced its support to the Baltics. Its European security and co-operation committee has issued a statement calling for Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia to be allowed into NATO at the Madrid summit in July.
- Baltic politicians evaluate the results of the Amsterdam EU summit.

- While meeting EU ambassadors, President Guntis Ulmanis criticised Prime Minister Andris Shkele for distancing himself from political parties in a recent TV adress. Ulmanis stressed that political parties were the backbone of democracy.
- The ministry of agriculture suggests special subsidies to young farmers under 30.
- Beginning June 20, the Russian Start transport company will start regular flights from Liepaja to Moscow.
